The state engine applies declarative YAML state files through these built-in modules. Each module manages one kind of resource idempotently — declare the desired state and the engine converges to it (and reports drift). See [Using State Management](../getting-started/) for the state-file language and workflow.

## System & core

- [`cmd`](cmd/) — Executes an arbitrary shell command via /bin/sh, gated by an idempotency guard (`creates`, `onlyif`, or `unless`).
- [`file`](file/) — Manages a single filesystem path — a regular file (content from inline text or a source), a directory, or a symlink — along with its owner, group, and mode.
- [`group`](group/) — Manages a Unix group, optionally pinning its numeric GID.
- [`hostname`](hostname/) — Manages the system static hostname.
- [`package`](package/) — Manages a Linux system package via the host's native package manager — present at any version or pinned to an exact one, or removed.
- [`service`](service/) — Manages a system service's running state and, optionally, its boot-enablement.
- [`system`](system/) — Manages system-level settings that don't fit the other stdlib modules — login banners (`/etc/motd`, `/etc/issue`, `/etc/issue.net`), marker-gated reboots, and the system locale.
- [`user`](user/) — Manages a Linux user account — its UID/GID, primary group, home directory, login shell, GECOS comment, and supplementary groups.

## Scheduled tasks

- [`at`](at/) — Manages one-shot scheduled jobs via the Linux `at` toolchain.
- [`cron`](cron/) — Manages a single per-user crontab entry, identified by the declaration name and tagged with a marker comment so only that entry is owned.
- [`systemd_timer`](systemd_timer/) — Manages a systemd `.timer` unit: it generates the unit from structured parameters and controls whether the timer is enabled at boot and currently armed.

## Storage

- [`disk`](disk/) — Manages the filesystem signature on a single block device: ensures a `/dev/` path carries the declared `fstype` (formatting it with `mkfs.<fstype>`) or has no signature at all.
- [`link`](link/) — Manages a symbolic or hard link at a path.
- [`lvm`](lvm/) — Manages one LVM object per declaration — a Physical Volume (`pv`), a Volume Group (`vg`), or a Logical Volume (`lv`).
- [`mount`](mount/) — Manages a filesystem's `/etc/fstab` entry and its live mount state.
- [`swap`](swap/) — Manages swap space — a swapfile or a swap partition/device — together with its /etc/fstab entry and live swapon state.

## Network (base)

- [`bond`](bond/) — Manages a Linux bonding (link-aggregation) interface — creates it at runtime via `ip link` with the declared mode, members, and link-monitor interval, with optional boot persistence to networkd or netplan.
- [`bridge`](bridge/) — Manages a Linux bridge interface at runtime via `ip link`, optionally enslaving member ports and persisting the bridge to the host network config.
- [`network`](network/) — Manages one network interface's runtime configuration — IP addresses, MTU, and admin up/down — via the iproute2 `ip` tool, optionally rendering a boot-survive file (systemd-networkd or netplan) so the config persists across reboot.
- [`route`](route/) — Manages one entry in the kernel routing table at runtime via iproute2, keyed on `(destination, table)` (plus `metric` when set).
- [`vlan`](vlan/) — Manages a Linux 802.1Q VLAN interface — creates or removes a tagged interface on a parent link at runtime via `ip link`, optionally persisting it to the host network config.

## Firewall (base)

- [`firewall`](firewall/) — Manages a single inbound allow rule for a named service or a port, dispatched to whichever firewall backend (iptables, nftables, or firewalld) is in use on the host.
- [`firewalld`](firewalld/) — Manages one item — a service, a port, or a rich rule — in a firewalld zone via `firewall-cmd --permanent`, reloading so the change takes effect.
- [`iptables`](iptables/) — Manages a single iptables (or ip6tables) rule, identified by its full spec (chain + match args + target) rather than a name.
- [`nftables`](nftables/) — Manages a single nftables rule inside an existing chain, identified by its canonical text (`family` + `table` + `chain` + `rule`).

## SSH & security

- [`security`](security/) — Manages SELinux settings (global mode and named booleans) and AppArmor per-profile modes.
- [`ssh`](ssh/) — Manages a single entry in a user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys — the classic authorized_key.present / .absent.

## System config

- [`kernel_module`](kernel_module/) — Manages a Linux kernel module: ensures it is loaded (or unloaded) and, by default, that a keystone-managed `/etc/modules-load.d` entry persists the choice across reboots.
- [`sysctl`](sysctl/) — Manages a kernel parameter (sysctl key): sets its runtime value and, by default, records it in a keystone-managed drop-in under /etc/sysctl.d/ so it survives a reboot.
- [`timezone`](timezone/) — Manages the system timezone.

## Files & VCS

- [`archive`](archive/) — Extracts an archive (tar, tar.gz, tar.bz2, or zip) into a target directory.
- [`config`](config/) — Manages a single key/value entry inside a config file — a flat `keyvalue` file or an INI file — touching only the line that defines the key and leaving every comment, blank line, and other key untouched.
- [`git`](git/) — Manages a git working tree on the agent: clones a repository to a path and optionally tracks a revision on the remote.
- [`langpkg`](langpkg/) — Manages one language-ecosystem package per declaration via pip, npm, or gem — distinct from the OS-level `package` module.

## Certificates

- [`x509`](x509/) — Manages a TLS certificate and its private key on disk (the declaration name is the certificate path) using crypto/x509 — no shelling out.
